references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, Moses warns against making carved images of any creature, which directly connects to the warning against making 'a carved image in the form of anything'.
Moses prophesies that the people will do evil after his death and provoke the Lord's anger by the work of their hands, reflecting the warning about doing what is evil in the Lord's sight.
Moses reminds them that the people did what was evil in the Lord's sight, using the same expression found in this warning.
Describes how the children of Israel actually did what was evil in the Lord's sight and served Baal, fulfilling the warning in Deuteronomy.
The second commandment forbids making carved images, which is the same prohibition Moses warns against breaking.
Jeroboam did what was evil in the Lord's sight by making cast images, a concrete fulfillment of the warning.
Describes how Israel abandoned the Lord's commands and made cast images, leading to the Lord's anger and exile.
Ezekiel describes idolatry and abominations that provoke the Lord, the same theme as the warning against provoking the Lord's anger.
